description: Gaia DR3 stars with a best-quality GSP-Spec metallicity, with the first 24 BP and 24 RP Hermite coefficients of their XP mean spectra, for a teaching demo that trains a small network in the browser.

selection.adql:
SELECT TOP 4000 gs.source_id, gs.random_index, gs.phot_g_mean_mag,
  ap.mh_gspspec, ap.teff_gspspec, ap.logg_gspspec, ap.flags_gspspec,
  xs.bp_n_relevant_bases, xs.rp_n_relevant_bases
FROM gaiadr3.gaia_source AS gs
JOIN gaiadr3.astrophysical_parameters AS ap ON ap.source_id = gs.source_id
JOIN gaiadr3.xp_summary AS xs ON xs.source_id = gs.source_id
WHERE ap.mh_gspspec IS NOT NULL
  AND ap.flags_gspspec LIKE '0000000000000%'
ORDER BY gs.random_index
selection.run_as: the same query restricted to consecutive random_index ranges of 250,000 (the archive stops anonymous queries after 60 s), scanned below random_index 4,250,000; the first 4000 rows in random_index order were kept
selection.adql_per_range:
SELECT gs.source_id, gs.random_index, gs.phot_g_mean_mag,
  ap.mh_gspspec, ap.teff_gspspec, ap.logg_gspspec, ap.flags_gspspec,
  xs.bp_n_relevant_bases, xs.rp_n_relevant_bases
FROM gaiadr3.gaia_source AS gs
JOIN gaiadr3.astrophysical_parameters AS ap ON ap.source_id = gs.source_id
JOIN gaiadr3.xp_summary AS xs ON xs.source_id = gs.source_id
WHERE ap.mh_gspspec IS NOT NULL
  AND ap.flags_gspspec LIKE '0000000000000%'
  AND gs.random_index >= {lo} AND gs.random_index < {hi}
ORDER BY gs.random_index
cuts: flags_gspspec characters 1 to 13 all '0' (best GSP-Spec quality, Recio-Blanco et al. 2023)
an XP continuous mean spectrum exists (join with gaiadr3.xp_summary)

coefficients.adql:
SELECT source_id, bp_n_parameters, rp_n_parameters, bp_coefficients, rp_coefficients, bp_coefficient_errors, rp_coefficient_errors
FROM gaiadr3.xp_continuous_mean_spectrum
WHERE source_id IN (<500 source_ids per query>)
coefficients.why_not_esa: the ESA TAP service does not expose this table; ESA serves it through DataLink, limited to 50 sources per anonymous request

features.normalisation: each coefficient divided by flux_scale = bp_coefficients[0] + rp_coefficients[0] of the same star, so the network sees spectral shape and not brightness
features.why_k: validation RMSE of a ridge fit and of a 32-32 tanh network on these stars stops improving near K = 24 (ridge 0.113 dex, network 0.114 dex, against 0.217 dex for predicting the training mean); more coefficients make the file larger and the small network overfit
features.storage: uint16 per feature: value = feature_offset + stored * feature_step (offsets and steps in the header)
features.browser_scaling: the page standardises each feature and the label with the mean and standard deviation of the training stars

split.rule: numpy.random.default_rng(20261025).permutation(n); the first 20 percent of that permutation is validation

columns.mh_gspspec: GSP-Spec [M/H] in dex, catalogue value (no calibration applied)

examples.rule: validation stars with Teff 4500 to 5000 K, log g 2 to 3 and a BP share of the flux, bp_coefficients[0] / flux_scale, within 0.02 of the median of that box (to keep strongly reddened stars out); the stars closest to the 3rd, 50th and 97th percentiles of [M/H] among them
examples.spectra: GaiaXPy 2.1.5 calibrate() on all 55 BP and 55 RP coefficients, 336 to 1020 nm in 2 nm steps, flux in W m^-2 nm^-1, four significant figures
